niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why You Like People Near You More
ideas.angle: The video explains the Propinquity Effect, where physical distance is the biggest predictor of friendship, surprising viewers by showing their 'choices' are just geography.

hook.en: Your best friend is just a coincidence.
hook.fr: Ton meilleur ami est juste une coincidence.

ideas.reason: Social dynamics and friendship hacks consistently go viral on TikTok and Shorts; the proximity effect is a counter-intuitive 'hard truth' that challenges personal agency.
sources: Festinger, Schachter, and Back (1950) - Social Pressures in Informal Groups

ideas.title: Why Your Brain Hates Unfinished Tasks
ideas.angle: It reveals why you can't stop thinking about an email you didn't send, showing how to use the Zeigarnik Effect to beat procrastination by just starting for 2 minutes.

hook.fr: Ton cerveau déteste les tâches inachevées.

ideas.reason: Productivity and 'brain hacks' are high-retention topics. Recent search trends show a spike in 'dopamine detox' and 'focus' queries in both English and French markets.
sources: Bluma Zeigarnik (1927) - On Finished and Unfinished Tasks

ideas.title: Nobody is Actually Judging You
ideas.angle: The video demonstrates the Spotlight Effect, proving people notice 50% less about your appearance or mistakes than you think, providing instant social anxiety relief.

hook.en: Stop worrying, nobody is watching you.
hook.fr: Arrête de t'inquiéter, personne ne te regarde.

ideas.reason: Mental health and self-improvement content is evergreen. This specific bias performs well because it offers a 'relief' payoff, encouraging viewers to share it with anxious friends.
sources: Gilovich, Medvec, and Savitsky (2000) - The Spotlight Effect in Social Judgment
